summary: A seat's delivery, read and close of graph mail can be recorded on its own host as local marks instead of lifecycle claims: a member alone does so at once, and a fleet of several members keeps writing claims until every member's message view and lists read marks, which a later release adds (db break-up step 4b, the writers)

replay.detail: Once marks are on (today: only on a member with no other members), this member writes no message.delivered, message.read or message.closed claim for a seat its own declarations place on it; it records a local mark instead (local_message_marks), which never replicates. A staging is still a message.staged claim: this build reads stagings recorded as marks (local_message_staged), and a later release records them once a release that reads them exists, so a rollback never offers staged mail again. Lifecycle claims already written keep counting, and readers take the further of a message's claims and marks. Persons, seats on other hosts, acted-for retired seats, delegated writes, native Claude-channel reads and delivery-probe mail (tagged delivery-probe, whose senders and doctor prove its read by the replicated claim) still write claims.

schema.detail: New member-local tables local_message_staged and local_message_mark_events, with their triggers; no change to any replicated table. Builds that read local_message_marks ignore both.

rules.detail: Marks are on only while every other current member, and every peer this daemon is configured with, advertises message_view_reads=1, read from each member's own newest daemon.started at its incarnation; ambiguous membership counts as not ready, and a member alone switches at once. No release advertises message_view_reads yet, this one included: it is advertised by the later release whose message view and lists ask a seat's host for its marks. Until every member runs that release, a fleet of several members keeps writing lifecycle claims exactly as before. The daemon decides it at startup and every minute, and doctor's message-marks check shows the decision and names the members that have not advertised message_view_reads. Every 4b-2 build advertises message_offsets=1, so other members ask it on the seat-freshness relay how far its seats got.

compatibility.detail: In a fleet of several members nothing changes: every member keeps writing lifecycle claims, because no member advertises message_view_reads yet, so every release reads every seat's lifecycle as before. A member with seat-freshness reads (v0.3.25 on) asks a marks-recording host in delivery status, doctor and the mail-backlog check, but its message view and lists read only its own records, where another host's mark would show as sent; that is why marks wait for message_view_reads. A member alone records its own seats' delivery, read and close as marks at once. Lifecycle requests (POST /v1/mailbox/receipts, POST /v1/messages/{id}/claims, cleanup, handoff acknowledgement) keep their request shapes; for a hosted seat's delivery, read or close recorded as a mark they answer the mark's offset-receipt, whose store_index is 0.

downtime.detail: No migration: the new tables are created empty, and marks start with the next lifecycle write once the barrier holds.

recovery.detail: A member that recorded marks (a member alone) can roll back to v0.3.25 or later safely: it reads the marks, offers nothing again, and writes claims from then on. Rolling it back to v0.3.24 or earlier shows mail delivered since then as undelivered, and its unread mail is redelivered once. A fleet of several members recorded no marks, so any rollback is as before. Version 4 backups with marks restore on any release that reads them (v0.3.25 on).
